Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Zenith Insurance Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Instructions for queuing your questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Zenith Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Investment Officer; and Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Zenith Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by robust new business production volume reaching record levels, solid reinsurance recoveries that bolstered our loss ratios, double-digit net written premiums growth across key lines of business, an improved investment income yield amid favorable rates, favorable changes in actuarial assumptions releasing prior reserves, and meaningful realized and unrealized gains on our investment portfolio. We are particularly excited about the initial success of our DriveSafe telematics product and its positive impact on risk selection and customer retention in personal auto lines.

Sarah, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $750 million, or $3.20 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included record new business production, strong reinsurance inflows, NWP expansion, enhanced investment yields, assumption updates, and investment gains. Our combined ratio was 92.4%. Investment income for the quarter was $1.92 billion, reflecting strong performance in our fixed income and alternatives segments. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with statutory surplus at $18.5 billion.

Let me dive deeper into these areas, starting with new business production volume, a key leading indicator of our top-line growth and long-term value creation. For the quarter ended September 30, 2024, we delivered record new business production of $2.8 billion in annualized premium equivalent across our core segments—up 18% year-over-year from $2.4 billion in Q3 2023. On a policy count basis, we wrote approximately 1.2 million new policies, a robust 22% increase year-over-year, reflecting strong consumer demand, disciplined pricing, and acceleration of our digital distribution initiatives.

Breaking it down by segment, our diversified portfolio continues to outperform peers in a hardening property and casualty market and resilient life demand. In property and casualty, new business hit $1.6 billion APE, up 25% year-over-year. Auto led at $850 million, up 28%, fueled by our Telematics-powered DriveSafe usage-based insurance product, which now accounts for 35% of new auto policies—up from 22% a year ago. Homeowners followed at $450 million, up 22%, benefiting from embedded policies-in-force growth in bundled offerings. Commercial lines contributed $300 million, up 20%, with specialty growth in cyber and directors and officers liability, where we captured 12% market share in mid-market cyber policies per AM Best data amid rising ransomware threats. Policy volume in P&C was 850,000 new policies, a 26% jump, with average premium per policy up 8% to $1,880, thanks to data-driven underwriting enhancements via AI models that reduced loss ratios by 150 basis points in new business cohorts.

In life and health, new business reached $1.2 billion APE, up 9% year-over-year, with present value of new business margins expanding 50 basis points to 28% due to an optimized mix toward higher-margin universal life and indexed universal life products. Term life annualized premium was $650 million, up 12%, bolstered by our direct-to-consumer digital platform generating 40% of sales at lower acquisition costs of 15% of APE versus industry averages. Group health added $350 million, up 5%, while critical illness riders saw 30% uptake. We issued 350,000 new life and health policies, up 14%, with value of new business totaling $420 million—a 12% increase—driven by improved lapse assumptions and longevity risk hedging through our partnership with Swiss Re.

Geographically, North America accounted for 72% of new business at $2.0 billion, up 20%, with U.S. personal lines surging on 9.5% average rate hikes in line with NAIC filings and California wildfire repricing. EMEA contributed 15% or $420 million, up 10%, led by UK motor renewal pricing and Nordic commercial expansion via our Aviva joint venture, hitting 150,000 policies. Asia-Pacific was 13% at $380 million, up 25%, propelled by India term life sales doubling to $120 million through our Bajaj Allianz tie-up and Hong Kong universal life demand. Emerging markets now represent 22% of total new business, up from 18%, with localized telematics and parametric products mitigating climate risks.

This performance highlights three trends: digital acceleration, where our InsureNow app and API integrations with fintechs like Lemonade and Root drove 55% of new business digitally, cutting agent costs by 20% and boosting conversion to 32%; pricing discipline achieving 10% net price realization through dynamic algorithms amid 6-8% industry increases per Verisk; and product innovation like parametric flood cover in Florida and EV-specific auto policies capturing 15% share in green niches. Challenges included competitive pressures in group health and softer European commercial renewals, but our new business combined ratio held at 92%, 300 basis points better than peers.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 new business to grow 15-20% year-over-year to $3.0 billion APE, supported by $500 million in capacity from our Munich Re quota share. We're doubling down on embedded insurance via Amazon and Uber partnerships, projecting 25% of 2024 new auto from these channels, adding 8-10% to next year's new business value and positioning for 14% ROE expansion.

Shifting to net written premiums, which grew 12.4% year-over-year to $4.2 billion—our strongest quarterly growth in three years—driven by disciplined rates, 89.2% retention, and new business flows, with organic growth at 11.1% excluding our Midwest Casualty Partners acquisition.

Personal lines led with 14.7% growth to $1.8 billion. Personal auto surged 16.2% to $1.1 billion on 9.8% renewal rates—above the 6-7% industry average per AM Best—and SummitDrive telematics now with 2.8 million policyholders, reducing auto loss ratios by 210 basis points to 68.4% and driving 22% new policies from younger segments via app quoting. Homeowners grew 11.9% to $700 million on 7.5% hikes amid Hurricane Beryl and Debby, with 91.5% retention via bundling and AI claims acceleration cutting settlements by 35%. Florida and Texas saw 18% growth through selective underwriting, while California grew 5% post-wildfire reforms.

Commercial lines grew 10.2% to $1.7 billion, focusing on middle-market. Workers' comp rose 12.8% to $650 million on 8.2% rates and light manufacturing expansion via ADP partnerships, with experience mod analytics pushing book-to-premium to 1.15x. General liability and umbrella grew 9.5% to $550 million on social inflation like talc litigation, with 15% umbrella attach rates. Commercial property was flat at 1.8% to $500 million, ceding more to Swiss Re post-wind events to protect our 92% combined ratio target. Northeast U.S. drove 13% growth, EMEA 7% on Brexit rates.

Specialty lines grew 13.9% to $700 million. Cyber exploded 28.4% to $250 million, outpacing Chubb and AIG amid 42% ransomware surge per Chainalysis, with parametric triggers and $400 million cat bonds limiting aggregation to 2.5% of surplus. D&O grew 11.2% to $200 million on SEC mandates and SPAC volatility, boosting premiums by 14%. Environmental and marine grew 8-10%, leveraging ESG products in Asia-Pacific.

This aligns with our Profitable Growth 2.0 strategy: shifting mix to specialty now 17% of NWP, investing $150 million in gen AI like PredictLoss flagging 25% more claims, and non-renewing $120 million underperformers to reallocate to high-ROE fleet telematics. We expect full-year NWP growth of 11-13%, with Q4 acceleration from commercial renewals and our Entrust portal.

On reinsurance recoveries, which played a pivotal role in our net loss ratio, we recognized $1.2 billion received in Q3, up 35% from $890 million last year. Year-to-date, cumulative recoveries are $2.1 billion, 72% of gross incurred losses from prior cats. This contributed to our 92.4% net combined ratio, down 480 basis points despite $3.4 billion gross losses from Hurricane Beryl and European windstorms.

Of Q3 recoveries, $850 million related to 2023 events, including $450 million accelerated for Hurricane Idalia via streamlined excess-of-loss towers. Our 2023 cat recovery rate is 78%, above our 70-75% target with 40% quota share on U.S. property.

Expected future recoveries: gross ultimate loss pick at $4.8 billion for 2024 YTD cats, with $2.9 billion recoverable over 12-18 months, including $1.6 billion probable maximum from property cat layers with Swiss Re, Munich Re, and Berkshire Hathaway Re. We anticipate 65% by year-end, 90% by mid-2025.

U.S. drove 55% at $660 million, Beryl netting $900 million at 64% post 50% quota with RenaissanceRe; California wildfires $280 million with Hannover Re parametrics expediting $120 million. Europe $320 million from Storm Hans analogs via 30% PartnerRe quota; Asia-Pacific lagged at 68% on typhoon disputes but unlocking $250 million via SCOR arbitration.

Our three-year recovery average improved to 76% from 68%, via RMS v18.1 cat modeling and AI claims triage reducing leakage 12%, plus January renewals with 25-40% rate hikes, 20% more reinstatement protection capping net retention at $400 million per event, and $500 million cat bonds.

We guide $4.5-5.0 billion total 2024 recoveries for $2.0 billion net cat loss after tax, supporting 93-95% full-year combined ratio, with reinsurers A+ rated and 92% collateralized.

Turning to investment income yield at 4.2% for the quarter, up 45 basis points year-over-year and 20 sequentially—our strongest since Q3 2021—on $184.5 billion average invested assets from P&C and life float. Net investment income hit $1.92 billion, up 12%, with new money at 5.1% and book yield at 4.0%.

Year-to-date average 4.1%, outpacing MetLife and Prudential, from overweight IG corporates at 4.8%, equity dividends adding 15 basis points from 12% allocation, and alternatives at 7.2% yield from REITs and Blackstone private credit.

Fixed income at 72%: 28% government/agency at 3.9%, 25% munis at tax-equivalent 6.5%, IG corporates. Duration 5.8 years, NAIC 1-rated 98%. U.S. 65% at 4.4%, Europe 20% at 3.6%, Asia-Pacific 15% at 4.8%.

We've optimized ALM with BlackRock Aladdin, executing $2.5 billion LDI, ramping ESG to 22% capturing greenium, trimming CCC paper, adding FRNs at SOFR+250bps. Guide 4.3-4.5% for 2025.

On realized and unrealized gains/losses: realized gains $285 million, up from $175 million, from $4.2 billion sales at 68 bps average gain. Fixed income $210 million trimming corporates as spreads tightened; equities $65 million from S&P trims; alternatives $10 million.

Unrealized net gains $620 million on AFS, flipping Q2 loss, from rate drops generating $450 million, tightening spreads $120 million, equity rally. YTD net gains $1.1 billion, ROE 4.9%. AOCI improved to -$2.8 billion.

ESG $12 billion allocation, AI LDI, 40% hedges, reinvestment ladder position us for 4.9-5.2% yields amid Fed cuts.

Finally, changes in actuarial assumptions yielded $175 million favorable, part of $285 million development contributing to operating income. Discount rates up 75 bps to 4.0% P&C/3.5% life/health reduced IBNR $72 million P&C, $23 million life via Bornhuetter-Ferguson and NCCI data.

Mortality A/E 92%, updating to 2020 CSO/VM-20 boosted DAC $28 million group life, longevity extension $17 million PRT. Morbidity up 8% added $18 million workers'/disability on 5.1% trends.

U.S. cats up 4% RMS assumptions offset by auto dev; Europe motor lapses better but morbidity up; Asia neutral.

AI stochastic modeling, AIR Touchstone climate integration, IFRS 17 ramp. Expect stability, Q4 sensitivities +100 bps rates $120 million tailwind.

David Patel: Thank you, Sarah. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our personal lines segment. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-enhanced telematics and parametric triggers.

Lisa Wong: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in investment-grade corporates and alternatives.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for queuing questions: press star then one on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from Jamie Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jamie Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the drivers behind the record new business volume?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Jamie. As Sarah detailed, it was broad-based: P&C up 25% led by DriveSafe in auto, life up 9% on digital term sales. Digital channels at 55%, pricing discipline, and emerging market push were key, with Q4 outlook strong.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Ruiz with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Ruiz: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of recent catastrophe activity on your business?

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning, Emily. Reinsurance recoveries mitigated it effectively—$1.2 billion in Q3 covered 72% YTD gross losses, keeping net combined at 92.4%. Our programs with Swiss Re and others position us well for ongoing activity.

Operator: Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel: What is the expected impact of potential regulatory changes around climate risk disclosure on your underwriting strategy?

David Patel: Good morning, Raj. We're ahead with AIR Touchstone integrations baking 15% higher PMLs into models, aligning with NAIC frameworks. It enhances selectivity in Florida/Gulf, supporting profitable growth without volume sacrifice.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Kim: On investments, how sustainable is the 4.2% yield?

Lisa Wong: Hi Lisa. Very sustainable—new money at 5.1%, barbell strategy with privates ramping to 12%. 2025 guide 4.3-4.5% assumes stable Treasuries; hedges protect against inversion.

Operator: Our next question from Mike Torres with Citigroup.

Mike Torres: Thoughts on NWP outlook amid softening rate signals?

Sarah Jenkins: Mike, supportive at 5-7% projected. Q4 11-13% FY growth from specialty/cyber momentum and digital broker onboarding. Vigilant on auto cycle.

Operator: That concludes the questions we have time for.

Michael Chen: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Zenith Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
